timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: We've got SaaS apps, Azure services, and old on-prem apps. One security plan for all?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: One strategy, three control planes: identity, network, and application.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: SSO for SaaS, RBAC for Azure at the narrowest scope, PIM for admin, Conditional Access for risky sign-ins.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Managed identities and workload identity federation. No passwords lying around.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Internet Access is a secure web gateway. Private Access is Zero Trust per-app access instead of a fat VPN.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So users don't get the whole network?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Correct. Just the apps they need. Private Link keeps PaaS traffic off the public internet too.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Defender for Cloud Apps. Shadow IT discovery, session controls, block risky uploads.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Application Proxy. MFA and device checks without rewriting the app.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Consent policies. High-privilege permissions require admin approval, not a user checkbox.
